extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), institutional Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX coordinator duties and measures
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes regulatory requirements in the Title IX final rule preamble concerning a Title IX Coordinator's obligations when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including notification, supportive measures, initiation of grievance procedures, and limits on action. Suitable for institutions implementing or auditing compliance with the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(f)(1) of the final regulations requires a Title IX Coordinator, when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part, to take the specific actions described in paragraph (f)(1) to promptly and effectively end any sex discrimination in the recipient's education program or activity, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects. Those actions are not required if the Title IX Coordinator reasonably determines, pursuant to paragraph (f)(2), that the conduct as alleged could not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires an initial, reasoned assessment of whether alleged conduct could constitute sex discrimination (i.e., plausibility). Affords recipients flexibility because the Title IX Coordinator may determine some reports do not warrant further action. Recipients are expected to train Title IX Coordinators to make these distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other appropriate prompt and effective steps regardless of complaint initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(f)(1)(vii) requires a Title IX Coordinator to take “other appropriate prompt and effective steps, in addition to steps necessary to effectuate the remedies provided to an individual complainant, if any, to ensure that sex discrimination does not continue or recur within the recipient's education program or activity,” and adds the phrase “Regardless of whether a complaint is initiated.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps are distinct from remedies to an individual complainant and must be prompt and effective. They are limited to non-disciplinary, non-punitive actions (e.g., educational programming, employee training, permitting a complainant to retake a class) so long as such measures are not imposed for punitive reasons and do not unreasonably burden a party. The provision clarifies a Coordinator must act even when no formal complaint exists, unless the Coordinator reasonably determines no action is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainant and respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(f)(1)(i) requires equitable treatment of the complainant and respondent, which encompasses communications with both parties, as warranted, to provide important information about a recipient's Title IX policies, obligations, and available resources and supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment pertains to both parties and does not require identical treatment of employee versus student respondents. It is distinct from the basic grievance-procedures notice requirements in §106.45(b)(1) and applies to obligations arising outside of or before grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of grievance procedures and informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(f)(1)(iii)(A)-(B), a Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant (or, if the complainant is unknown, the individual who reported the conduct) about the recipient's grievance procedures and the availability of an informal resolution process if available and appropriate; and must notify a respondent of those procedures and processes if a complaint is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the complainant is unknown, notifying the reporter is permitted to help identify the complainant. Providing only broken web links does not satisfy the notice requirement. Recipients may provide written notice to respondents when a complaint is initiated, but the Department declines to require written notice in every case. Parental notification of minors is governed by state/local law or school policy, not by this federal requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer and coordination of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(f)(1)(ii) requires a recipient to require its Title IX Coordinator to offer and coordinate supportive measures, if appropriate, for a complainant upon notice of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; and to offer and coordinate supportive measures for a respondent when the recipient has initiated grievance procedures or has offered the respondent an informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be offered “as appropriate” (the regulation aligns the timing for respondents with initiation of grievance procedures or offer of informal resolution to avoid premature notification). Supportive measures are non-disciplinary, not imposed for punitive reasons, may not unreasonably burden either party, are subject to the burdens limits in §106.44(g)(2), and may be challenged under §106.44(g)(4). The Department clarified that supportive measures are intended to restore access, and removed language implying a need to preliminarily determine respondent culpability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of grievance procedures and informal resolution processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(f)(1)(iv) requires a Title IX Coordinator to initiate a recipient's informal resolution process under §106.44(k) if it is available, appropriate, and requested by all parties; and to initiate grievance procedures in accordance with §106.45 (and, if applicable, §106.46) when a complainant wishes to initiate a complaint or when the Title IX Coordinator initiates a complaint under §106.44(f)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation of grievance procedures triggers the procedural protections and limitations in §§106.45/106.46, including the rule that disciplinary sanctions may be imposed only after the recipient complies with those grievance-procedure requirements. The Coordinator's pre-initiation steps (f)(1)(i)-(iii) help determine whether to initiate a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment standard: conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations use the standard “conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination” to trigger the Title IX Coordinator's duties; the Coordinator must assess whether reported conduct could plausibly constitute sex discrimination and may reasonably determine that some reports, even if true, could not constitute sex discrimination (e.g., do not involve differential treatment on the basis of sex or sex-based harassment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is intended to avoid requiring action for every report regardless of plausibility, while ensuring coordinators act on reports that could reasonably allege sex discrimination. Training is expected so coordinators can distinguish plausible allegations from those that cannot constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective response standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'prompt and effective' response to sex discrimination is required — a standard familiar from prior Department regulations and enforcement, and consistent with courts' consideration of deliberate indifference (e.g., showing liability when there is a delayed, inadequate, or ineffective response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding promptly and effectively may require timely action, avoiding lengthy or unjustified delays, and taking measures adequate to stop discrimination and prevent recurrence. The Department references case law (e.g., Cianciotto; Zeno) and analogizes to other civil rights statutes requiring similar responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Title IX Coordinator authority (no discipline or undue burden outside grievance procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions a Title IX Coordinator may take outside of initiated grievance procedures under §106.44(f) must not include disciplinary sanctions and must not include supportive measures that unreasonably burden any party; nothing in §106.44(f) permits a Coordinator to circumvent the grievance-procedure requirements of §§106.45/106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Coordinator determines disciplinary sanctions may be required, the recipient must initiate grievance procedures and follow §§106.45/106.46 before imposing sanctions. Measures under (f)(1)(vii) should be non-disciplinary (educational programming, training, remedial steps) and must not be punitive or unreasonably burden a complainant or respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, delegation, and technical assistance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department expects recipients to adequately train their Title IX Coordinators to distinguish allegations that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination from those that could not, and authorizes recipients to permit their Title IX Coordinators to delegate duties. The Department will offer technical assistance as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are responsible for equipping Coordinators and employees to meet the regulatory duties, including by training and allowing delegation where appropriate. The Department views expanded reporting and Coordinator responsibilities as necessary to ensure nondiscrimination and will provide assistance to promote compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with law enforcement and timing of notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department clarifies that delays in notifying a respondent may be justified in circumstances involving a concurrent criminal investigation; §§106.45(b)(4) and 106.46(e)(5) permit reasonable extensions of timeframes on a case-by-case basis for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays are not required by the Title IX provisions, but a concurrent law enforcement investigation may justify delaying notification to avoid compromising the criminal process. Recipients should evaluate such circumstances case-by-case and document good cause for extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and limits of 'supportive measures'
rubrics_metrics.description: The final definition of 'supportive measures' maintains the intent to provide non-disciplinary, non-punitive measures that restore access to education without presuming respondent culpability. The Department removed language suggesting supportive measures should 'deter the respondent' and removed 'temporary measures that burden a respondent that are designed to protect the safety of the complainant,' replacing it with reference to 'measures that are designed to protect the safety of the parties.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures may be offered but recipients are not required to provide every possible measure. All supportive measures are subject to limits in §106.44(g)(2), may be challenged under §106.44(g)(4), and may not be imposed for punitive or disciplinary purposes. These edits were made to avoid any implication of bias against respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance expectation and enforcement avenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are expected to comply with the Title IX regulations; failure of a Title IX Coordinator or employees to take actions required under §106.44(f)(1) (including prompt and effective actions under (f)(1)(vii)) would result in noncompliance. Anyone who believes a recipient's treatment of a complainant or respondent constitutes sex discrimination may file a complaint with OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will evaluate complaints and, if appropriate, investigate and resolve matters consistent with the regulations. Recipients should ensure policies, training, and practices align with regulatory duties to avoid enforcement actions.
